trust_decision.summary: The dedupe key for a unique job is md5(class . method . json_encode(data)), decided in one function, QueueManager::getUniqueId(). At the pinned commit sort($data) sorts by value and reindexes, so key/value association is discarded: ['a'=>1,'b'=>2] and ['a'=>2,'b'=>1] both hash as [1,2], and ['k'=>'admin','r'=>'guest'] collides with any other payload with the same value multiset. The second push is then silently ignored (Cache::read hit at line 251), so a legitimate job is dropped. The published fix replaces the value-sort with a recursive key-sort (ksort) so the identity depends on keys as well as values.

landing_point.why: The advisory names getUniqueId, and sort($data) is the only normalisation between the caller's payload and the md5 at line 315; it is also the only place in the repository where a job's dedupe key is derived.

fix_sites.entry_point: QueueManager::push() public static API (reached directly by applications, by Cake\Queue\Mailer\Transport\QueueTransport::send(), by Cake\Queue\Mailer\QueueTrait::push() and by the `bin/cake queue requeue` CLI); the method itself, QueueManager::getUniqueId(), is also a public static API
fix_sites.module_kind: core library service, root namespace, public static API

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Both the push side and the consumption side call the same getUniqueId() helper, so a solver will argue the key is identical by construction and the delete path (Consumption/) needs no change of its own.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Payloads that differ only in key insertion order must still collapse to one queue entry: ['a'=>1,'b'=>2] and ['b'=>2,'a'=>1] have to hash the same, or shouldBeUnique queues duplicates. An over-broad fix that hashes the payload as given (json_encode/serialize without normalising) breaks exactly this.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: src/QueueManager.php:307 (the normalisation that must stay) and tests/TestCase/QueueManagerTest.php:190-206 (testUniqueMessageIsQueuedOnlyOnce)

O6_input_shapes: associative arrays whose keys differ but whose value multiset is identical: ['user_id'=>'admin','role'=>'guest'] vs ['foo'=>'admin','bar'=>'guest'] (fix.diff:72-78)
associative arrays with the same keys and permuted values: ['a'=>1,'b'=>2] vs ['a'=>2,'b'=>1] (fix.diff:68-70)
the same key/value pairs in different insertion order, which must stay equal (fix.diff:65-66)
nested arrays with reordered keys, requiring the sort to recurse (fix.diff:80-82)
list arrays, where the fixed behaviour is that [1,2,3] and [3,2,1] are now DIFFERENT because sorting is by key not value (fix.diff:51-53)
